verdict.rationale: LM Studio's own docs show GPU offload control (`lms load --gpu`) and two inference engines, llama.cpp and Apple MLX, where MLX is vendor-specific acceleration for Apple Silicon. A community comment also implies a CUDA acceleration setting exists. There is no first-party documentation of NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm/Vulkan, or other vendor kernels, and one user says AMD support is not seamless. That is a general wish rather than a concrete failure, so it lowers confidence but does not make this disputed. Missing for 10: first-party docs on NVIDIA CUDA runtime support, AMD ROCm/Vulkan kernel support, other GPU vendors, how to select a backend per vendor, and hands-on corroboration on non-Apple GPUs.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can run models on NVIDIA, AMD, or other GPU vendors using vendor-specific acceleration kernels

citations.quote: Now that LM Studio supports MLX models, it's one of the most efficient too.
